narration:
One point four percent of Console users who linked providers may have had keys exposed.
So an AI coding tool can become a credit-card risk without seeing your card.
OpenCode said an intruder reached a legacy system,
where OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google keys may have been exposed.
In football, whoever holds the equipment-room key can enter,
so a digital key carries real authority.
An API key is a digital spending key sent with each request.
It identifies the project and attaches usage to billing.
That means it usually cannot open your whole account,
but it can spend through the project it controls.
The problem is, a thief can run requests,
drain quotas, interrupt your code, or create charges.
So treat an exposed key as compromised, and revoke it
then check billing, replace it, and update the tool.
After that, test the old key, set low limits,
separate tools, restrict Google keys.
And follow the channel, because we explain security problems before they reach your bill.
Because one football key should never open the whole stadium,
would you trust an AI coding tool with your payment credentials?

research.summary:
An AI coding tool can become a credit-card risk when it stores a user’s third-party API key. In the reported OpenCode Console incident, an intruder accessed a legacy system and provider keys saved by some users may have been exposed; the reported affected group was 1.4% of Console users who had linked outside providers. ([thehackernews.com](https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/opencode-console-breach-may-have.html?utm_source=openai))

An API key is best understood as a digital spending key: software sends it with requests, and the provider uses it to identify the project or account, apply quotas, and—when billing is enabled—charge usage to the associated account. A stolen key may let someone run large numbers of model requests, exhaust quotas, generate unexpected charges, or interrupt legitimate access. It usually is not the same as a password granting access to your entire account; its danger is the authority and billing attached to the specific API project or workspace. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5112595-best-practices-for-api-key-safet?utm_source=openai))

Ordinary users should treat a potentially exposed key as compromised: revoke or disable it immediately, inspect provider usage and billing for suspicious activity, create a replacement, update the coding tool or environment with the new key, and then verify that the old key no longer works. OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google all document key rotation or deletion procedures. ([help.openai.com](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5112595-best-practices-for-api-key-safet?utm_source=openai))

Also reduce the blast radius. Use separate keys or projects for separate tools, restrict Google keys to the required APIs and applications or IPs, and set the lowest practical spend, quota, or usage caps. OpenAI provides project and organization spend limits; Google provides project spend caps and quotas, though Google warns that billing data and long-running tasks can create delays or overages. ([developers.openai.com](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/spend-limits?utm_source=openai))

Would you trust an AI coding tool with your payment credentials?

claims.claim: OpenCode’s reported incident involved a legacy system, and provider API keys saved in Console workspaces may have been exposed; the reported affected population was 1.4% of Console users who had linked an outside provider.
claims.source_title: OpenCode Console Breach May Have Exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API Keys

claims.claim: A compromised OpenAI API key can cause unexpected charges, quota depletion, data loss, and interruption of API access.
claims.source_title: Best Practices for API Key Safety

claims.claim: OpenAI recommends immediately rotating a key believed to have leaked and updating production applications to use the replacement.
claims.source_title: Best Practices for API Key Safety

claims.claim: Anthropic describes API keys as bearer credentials used in request authorization and recommends storing them securely and disabling or deleting keys suspected of being leaked.

Google standard API keys associate requests with a project for billing and quota purposes, while Google recommends restricting keys by API and by application, IP address, or other permitted client type.
claims.source_title: Manage API keys; Best practices for securely using API keys

claims.claim: OpenAI has organization- and project-level spend limits that can cause requests to fail once a configured hard limit is reached.

Google AI Studio supports project-level and billing-account spend caps for the Gemini API, but Google warns that billing data may be delayed and some long-running tasks can create overages beyond a project cap.
Google recommends creating a replacement key, updating applications and deployment configurations, testing the replacement, and then deleting or revoking the old key.

metadata.title: OpenCode Breach: AI API Keys Could Drain Your Budget
metadata.description:
A security breach involving OpenCode Console may have exposed OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google API keys linked by about 1.4% of users. This short explains why an API key can create usage charges without giving someone access to your full account.

If you stored a provider key in OpenCode Console, revoke and replace it, review billing, set spending limits, and update connected tools. One digital key should never unlock the whole stadium.
